claim: No test updates a draft's paid_amount to exactly the sum of its saved allocations, so refusing that allowed case (`allocated >= inputs.paid_amount` instead of `>`) goes unnoticed.
evidence: REQ-007-PRS-F005 (docs/specs/req-007-*.md lines 113 and 121): the allocations together are at most the paid amount, for an update giving no references the draft's as saved; only lowering paid_amount below the saved allocations is refused. src/enterich/tools/bank_and_cash.py line 559 holds the comparison. tests/integration/test_bank_and_cash_drafts.py covers only the two sides: line 671 `update(mcp, paid_amount=70)` against 80 allocated (refused) and line 794 `update(mcp, paid_amount=100)` against 80 allocated (accepted); none gives 80. The same boundary on the create path (`_check_references`, line 352) has no survivor.
proposal: In tests/integration/test_bank_and_cash_drafts.py, beside the test at line 671: on the draft with 80 allocated, `update(mcp, paid_amount=80)` without references succeeds, the saved draft has paid_amount and received_amount 80, and the result carries no advance warning (fully allocated, REQ-007-PRS-F007).

verdict.reason: Refuted: an end-to-end test already asserts the boundary case. The mutant is real and not equivalent (src/enterich/tools/bank_and_cash.py:559, `allocated > inputs.paid_amount` to `>=`), and the finding is right that the integration tests only cover the two sides (tests/integration/test_bank_and_cash_drafts.py:671 gives 70 against 80 allocated, :794 gives 100). But tests/e2e/test_drafts.py:613-648 (test_create_and_update_draft_payment_entry) creates a draft with paid_amount 30 and one reference allocating 20, then at :644-647 calls update_draft_payment_entry with only paid_amount "20" and no references, takes `.data` (which asserts `not self.error`, tests/integration/mcp.py:44-46) and asserts `(updated["unallocated_amount"], updated["warnings"]) == (0, [])` at :648. That is exactly paid_amount equal to the saved allocations, accepted, with no advance warning; under the mutant the update would be refused and this test would fail. The mutant survives only because the mutation run does not run tests/e2e (it needs a live ERPNext site); the end-to-end tests are a gate of the project (ADR-008 line 11 and 108, harness/README.md step 8). I did not run the e2e test against the mutant (no site in this step); the conclusion is from reading the code. The proposed integration test would duplicate the e2e assertion on the fake rather than close an unasserted behaviour.

claim: No test checks that a purchase invoice create's duplicate refusal and warning say which of the two matches of REQ-005-PRS-F006 fired (bill number against a draft or submitted purchase invoice, or supplier, posting date and items against a draft); they check only the matching document's name.
evidence: src/enterich/tools/procure_to_pay.py lines 343-358 choose (match, kind) per branch and pass them to drafts.refuse_duplicates / drafts.duplicate_warning. With the mutants the text reads "a None with the same ...", "with the same None", or, in the bill branch, "a draft with the same supplier and bill_no" for a submitted invoice (mutmut_89, mutmut_108 fall back to the default kind "draft"). tests/integration/test_procure_to_pay_drafts.py: test_a_recorded_supplier_invoice_is_refused_naming_it (startswith "allow_duplicate:" and the name), test_allow_duplicate_records_the_bill_again_and_says_so, test_a_create_sent_again_is_refused_naming_the_first_draft, test_without_a_bill_the_items_match, test_allow_duplicate_on_the_item_match_warns all assert only the name. The spec requires only that matches and allow_duplicate are named (REQ-001-PRS-F005), so the text of what matched is the code's own contract; the sales side pins it in full (tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py line 346). Not included as wording-only noise: mutmut_57, mutmut_58 ("draft" literal), mutmut_6 (what=None). Equivalent: mutmut_19 (taxes "" is read only as `taxes or []`).
proposal: In tests/integration/test_procure_to_pay_drafts.py assert the full text for both branches, refused and allowed: with bill_no R-4711, the error equals "allow_duplicate: a purchase invoice with the same supplier and bill_no exists (ACC-PINV-2026-00001). Check it first; ..." and the warning with allow_duplicate equals "Possible duplicate of ACC-PINV-2026-00001: a purchase invoice with the same supplier and bill_no."; with items=DRAFT_ITEMS and no bill_no, the same with "a draft with the same supplier, posting date and items".

verdict.reason:
Confirmed, with one part of the claim narrowed: the end-to-end tests already pin the bill-number branch, but nothing pins the item branch, and no test in the unit/integration gate pins either. I did not run a throwaway test against the mutants; the verdict rests on reading the code, the mutant diffs and every assertion on this text under tests/.

Code: src/enterich/tools/procure_to_pay.py:343-348 sets (match, kind) to (BILL_MATCH, "purchase invoice") or (DRAFT_MATCH, "draft") and passes them at :356 (refuse_duplicates) and :358 (duplicate_warning). src/enterich/tools/drafts.py:98-106 builds "allow_duplicate: a {kind} with the same {match} exists (...)" and "Possible duplicate of ...: a {kind} with the same {match}."

Mutants (mutmut show): 85/104 pass match=None, 86/105 pass kind=None, 88/107 pass kind in place of match, 89/108 drop kind so it defaults to "draft". None is equivalent as a whole: each changes the text in at least the bill branch. 89 and 108 are equivalent only in the item branch, where kind is already "draft".

Integration tests (tests/integration/test_procure_to_pay_drafts.py): :330 and :372 assert only startswith("allow_duplicate:") plus the document name; :351-355 and :719-722 assert only that the name is in the warning. No unit test touches this text.

End-to-end (tests/e2e/test_drafts.py:356-373): the refusal must start with "allow_duplicate: a purchase invoice with the same supplier and bill_no exists (" and the warning must end with ": a purchase invoice with the same supplier and bill_no." That would kill all eight mutants in the bill branch. It does not refute the finding because:
- No test anywhere asserts "a draft with the same supplier, posting date and items" for a purchase invoice (grep over tests/ finds that wording only for sales, at tests/e2e/test_drafts.py:263 and tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py:346). Under 85, 86, 88, 104, 105 and 107 the item branch reads "with the same None", "a None with" or "a draft with the same draft" and every test passes.
- The e2e suite is skipped without E2E_ERPNEXT_URL, runs weekly and is not a required check (docs/guides/development.md:103); pyproject.toml:74 excludes it from the mutation run.

Required and observable: REQ-001-PRS-F005 (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:254) requires only naming the matches and allow_duplicate, and REQ-005-PRS-F006 (docs/specs/req-005*.md:116) defines the two matches. The text saying which match fired is tool output the agent reads, and the sales side and the e2e test already treat it as contract. A test in the existing module closes it with no spec or code change, so the class is fix.

Pattern: refusal-by-prefix fits the refusal half directly (:330 and :372 check the start and the name, not what matched). The warning half is the same gap, checked by "in" rather than by prefix.

Fix scope: full-text equality for refusal and warning in both branches, as the finding proposes, in tests/integration/test_procure_to_pay_drafts.py.

claim: No test checks that a return create's duplicate refusal or warning says what matched and what the match is (a draft return against the same invoice, or a purchase invoice with the same supplier and bill_no).
evidence: src/enterich/tools/returns.py line 223 builds Match(names, RETURN_MATCH, "draft return"); src/enterich/tools/procure_to_pay.py line 435 builds Match(names, BILL_MATCH, "purchase invoice"). With the mutants the text reads "a draft return with the same None exists" or "a None with the same ...". tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py: test_a_draft_return_against_the_invoice_is_a_duplicate, test_a_draft_debit_note_against_the_invoice_is_a_duplicate, test_a_debit_note_sent_again_is_refused_naming_the_first_draft and test_allow_duplicate_creates_and_warns assert the prefix and the name only; test_a_debit_note_with_a_known_number_is_a_duplicate adds "bill_no" in the text, which kills a None match but not a None kind. Also covers REQ-004-PRS-F008 for the sales side. The spec states only that the match is named, so the rest of the text is the code's own contract. Judged equivalent or noise in returns.py: x__plain__mutmut_2/17 (cast), x_rows__mutmut_16/35/87 (sum of Decimals without a start differs only for an empty sequence, where the int 0 compares the same and .quantize is unreachable for an invoice without rows), x_invoice_of__mutmut_23/25/28 (ERPNext always returns docstatus), x_invoice_of__mutmut_46 and x_rows__mutmut_47/48/49 (wording), x_invoice_of__mutmut_6 and x_editable__mutmut_6 (what=None, wording).
proposal: In tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py assert the whole text: the sales and purchase refusals equal "allow_duplicate: a draft return with the same invoice (return_against) exists (<draft name>). Check it first; ...", the allowed create's warning equals "Possible duplicate of <draft name>: a draft return with the same invoice (return_against).", and the debit note with bill_no CN-77 is refused with "a purchase invoice with the same supplier and bill_no exists (ACC-PINV-2026-00009)".

verdict.reason:
Confirmed; I could not refute it. The three mutants are not equivalent: src/enterich/tools/returns.py:223 builds Match(names, RETURN_MATCH, "draft return") and src/enterich/tools/procure_to_pay.py:435 builds Match(names, BILL_MATCH, "purchase invoice"), and both feed the user-visible text in src/enterich/tools/drafts.py:98-106 ("allow_duplicate: a {kind} with the same {match} exists (...)" and "Possible duplicate of ...: a {kind} with the same {match}."). With the mutants the refusal and the warning read "a None with the same ..." or "a draft return with the same None". mutmut results lists all three as survived; I did not write a throwaway test, the survival follows from the recorded status and the assertions below.

No existing test checks this text for a return create. In tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py the refusals at lines 352-353, 517-518, 548-549 assert only startswith("allow_duplicate: ") and the draft's name; the warning tests at lines 373-376 and 1071-1072 assert only the name; line 1045-1047 adds "bill_no" in the text, which pins BILL_MATCH but not the kind. In tests/e2e/test_drafts.py:545-548 the sales return refusal is again prefix plus name; lines 367-373 assert the full "a purchase invoice with the same supplier and bill_no" text, but for create_draft_purchase_invoice (procure_to_pay.py:344/392), a different code path from the return's same_bill at line 435. No e2e test covers a purchase return duplicate.

The behaviour is observable (refusal text and warnings reach the MCP client) and inside the current specs: REQ-001-PRS-F005 (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:256) requires naming the matching documents, REQ-005-PRS-F009 (docs/specs/req-005*.md:169-178) and REQ-004-PRS-F008 define the return matches. A test asserting the whole text closes it with no spec or code change, so class fix. The same full-text assertion already exists for other creates (tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py:346, tests/e2e/test_drafts.py:263-268), so the proposal matches the suite's convention. Pattern refusal-by-prefix fits: the refusal is checked by its start and the name, not by what matched.

claim: No test checks that the warning of an update giving an already recorded bill_no (purchase invoice and purchase return) says it is a purchase invoice with the same supplier and bill_no; only the other document's name is asserted.
evidence: src/enterich/tools/procure_to_pay.py lines 391-393 and 470-472: drafts.duplicate_warning(matches, BILL_MATCH, "purchase invoice"). Mutants give "a purchase invoice with the same None", "a None with the same supplier and bill_no", "a draft with the same purchase invoice" (mutmut_78, mutmut_58) or "a draft with the same supplier and bill_no" (mutmut_79, mutmut_59) although the match may be a submitted invoice. tests/integration/test_procure_to_pay_drafts.py::test_an_update_to_a_recorded_bill_warns and tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py::test_a_debit_note_update_with_a_known_number_warns assert only the name in the warning (REQ-005-PRS-F009 for the return). Equivalent in the same functions: x_update_draft_purchase_invoice__mutmut_21 (taxes ""), mutmut_42 and x_update_draft_purchase_return__mutmut_22 (matches None is read only for truth); noise: x_update_draft_purchase_invoice__mutmut_6 (what=None, wording).
proposal: In both tests assert the warning in full: warning == "Possible duplicate of ACC-PINV-2026-00001: a purchase invoice with the same supplier and bill_no." for update_draft_purchase_invoice, and the same with ACC-PINV-2026-00009 for update_draft_purchase_return.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed for the purchase return half only; the purchase invoice half is already asserted end to end. I read the code, tests and specs and the mutant diffs; I did not run a throwaway test against the mutants.

Code: src/enterich/tools/procure_to_pay.py:391-393 (update_draft_purchase_invoice) and :470-472 (update_draft_purchase_return) both call drafts.duplicate_warning(matches, BILL_MATCH, "purchase invoice"). src/enterich/tools/drafts.py:105-106 formats it as "Possible duplicate of {names}: a {kind} with the same {match}." with kind defaulting to "draft". `mutmut show` gives the mutants as described: BILL_MATCH -> None ("with the same None"), kind -> None ("a None with"), BILL_MATCH dropped ("a draft with the same purchase invoice"), kind dropped ("a draft with the same supplier and bill_no"). None is equivalent: each changes the text returned in `warnings` and written to the draft's comment.

Purchase invoice update (mutants _75, _76, _78, _79): refuted. tests/e2e/test_drafts.py:396-421 (test_update_draft_purchase_invoice_to_a_known_bill_no_warns) asserts warning.startswith("Possible duplicate of <seeded invoice>") and warning.endswith(": a purchase invoice with the same supplier and bill_no."), which fails on all four. They survive only because the mutation run does not run tests/e2e. tests/integration/test_procure_to_pay_drafts.py:657-660 asserts only the name.

Purchase return update (mutants _55, _56, _58, _59): confirmed. tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py:1075-1080 (test_a_debit_note_update_with_a_known_number_warns) asserts only "ACC-PINV-2026-00009" in warning. tests/e2e has no update_draft_purchase_return bill_no case: its only mentions are tests/e2e/seed.py:92 and tests/e2e/test_rights.py:221, which sends remarks only. No other test in tests/ asserts the wording for this tool.

Requirement: REQ-005-PRS-F009 (docs/specs/req-005, line 171 and DoD line 178) says an update giving such a bill_no "warns naming it", where the match is "another draft or submitted purchase invoice ... [with] the same supplier and bill_no". The spec does not fix the wording, but a warning calling a possibly submitted invoice "a draft", or saying "the same None", is observable and wrong against that description. A full-string assertion in the existing integration test closes it within the current specs, so class is fix.

Pattern: none fits. This is a warning, not a refusal, and it is checked by a contained name, not by its start; no argument sent to ERPNext is involved.

Test file: only tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py is needed. The fix agent could also tighten tests/integration/test_procure_to_pay_drafts.py:660 so the four invoice mutants stop resurfacing in mutation runs, but that half is not a gap under the e2e rule, so I left it out.
